primitives.name: Disguised Play Arrangement
primitives.verbatim_quote: To disguise a play, the simplest method is to study out an arrangement of men of such a nature that the resulting move—the final outlet for the runner—may be varied without alteration in the first formation.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes fixed initial formation geometry, opponent ignorance of signal, and perfect execution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if opponents learn the signal pattern or disrupt the initial formation.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction regions via geometric uncertainty sets.
layer2.telemetry: Observed variance in final outlet distribution relative to expected.

primitives.name: Wedge Formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Thus a wedge may be formed which shall start forward with the runner in the center and yet let him out either directly in front or at one side or the other.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes linear force propagation through the wedge structure and predictable exit points.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under high defensive pressure or miscommunication among blockers.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSE state-transition logic where initial configuration dictates multiple action paths.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of intended versus actual exit direction.

primitives.name: Signal-Based Decision
primitives.verbatim_quote: The signal given when the wedge is forming indicates to the runner and his assistants which outlet will be used, and the opponents are utterly unable from the position of the men to tell which the outlet will be.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes noiseless signaling channel and opponent inability to decode based on visible positions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates if signals leak through body language or if opponents adopt counter-signal strategies.

layer2.mapping: Relates to GSI hypothesis testing where signals serve as informative priors.
layer2.telemetry: Probability of correct signal decoding by offensive and defensive units.

primitives.name: Criss-Cross Pass
primitives.verbatim_quote: The criss-cross or double pass is another excellent example of a disguised play,
primitives.assumptions: Assumes precise timing between passes and unpredictable receiver selection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses if receivers do not read the play correctly or if defenders anticipate the pattern.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE sequential decision trees with hidden information states.
layer2.telemetry: Completion ratio of passes within the criss-cross sequence.
